definition: The paired female gonads that produce ova and secrete sex hormones; standard Polish clinical and lay term for ovaries.
The paired tubes connecting the ovaries to the uterus through which ova travel after ovulation; fallopian tubes.
notes: Anatomical concept absent from the canonical registry; the English equivalent is unambiguous; low lay recognition outside biology/medical education contexts.

definition: Either of two small glands at the vaginal introitus that secrete lubricating mucus during sexual arousal; Bartholin's gland.
notes: Eponymous term after Caspar Bartholin the Younger; singular form used in Polish for each gland individually; recognition limited to medical and sex-education contexts.

definition: The paired ducts that transport sperm from the epididymis to the ejaculatory duct during ejaculation; vas deferens.
notes: Low lay recognition; primarily encountered in biology curricula and vasectomy-related health communication; 'nasienie' means semen/seed.

definition: The gland in the male reproductive system that produces part of seminal fluid; prostate.
notes: Latin/Greek loanword; high recognition driven by widespread prostate cancer public health campaigns in Poland; also used in erotic contexts re: prostate stimulation.

definition: The dominant formal Polish term for sexual intercourse; used in law, medicine, sex education, and journalism.
notes: 'Płciowy' derives from 'płeć' (sex/gender); 'stosunek' literally means 'relation' or 'ratio'; the compound is the near-universal clinical default.

definition: Literally 'sexual co-living'; a formal yet gentle Polish euphemism for sexual intercourse that foregrounds relational cohabitation over the physical act.
notes: Softer register than 'stosunek płciowy'; preferred in pastoral, religious, and polite journalistic contexts; 'współżycie' alone (without 'seksualne') can mean civic coexistence, requiring the qualifier for disambiguation.

definition: Clinical and zoological Latin loanword for copulation; used in biological and sexological Polish more than in everyday speech.
notes: Sounds more academic and distancing than 'stosunek płciowy'; frequent in animal-behavior writing and formal sexology; can carry a faintly dehumanizing or detached tone when applied to humans.

definition: Direct borrowing of Latin 'coitus'; the clinical term for penile-vaginal intercourse used primarily in Polish medical and sexological literature.
notes: More technical and narrower than 'stosunek płciowy'; implies specifically PIV intercourse; recognition lower than 'kopulacja' because it is less common even in educational texts.

definition: The insertion of a penis, finger, or object into a bodily orifice for sexual purposes; Polish clinical and journalistic term for penetration.
notes: Slightly more visceral than 'stosunek płciowy' due to its focus on the physical mechanics; widely used in journalism, erotica, and sex-positive educational content.

definition: Literally 'genital act'; a formal Polish term for the act of sexual intercourse, frequently used in criminal law and church documents.
notes: 'Płciowy' (from 'płeć') has a stronger gender/sex connotation than 'seksualny'; predominates in Polish legal language (e.g., Kodeks karny) and Catholic moral theology.

definition: Literally 'sexual act'; a broad clinical term for any sexual activity, often used interchangeably with 'akt płciowy' but technically wider in scope.
notes: 'Seksualny' is a Latinate borrowing sounding more modern than 'płciowy'; preferred in psychology, sociology, and media; scope includes non-PIV acts more naturally than 'akt płciowy'.

definition: Literally 'coming closer' or 'approach'; the most common single-word Polish euphemism for sexual intercourse, foregrounding emotional and physical closeness.
notes: Polysemous: also means political rapprochement and camera close-up; the sexual reading is entirely context-dependent; preferred in romantic, religious, and polite journalistic registers.

definition: Literally 'bodily approach/closeness'; a formal Polish euphemism for sexual intercourse that adds a somatic qualifier to plain 'zbliżenie'.
notes: 'Cielesny' (bodily/carnal) carries an ecclesiastical resonance echoing the Latin 'carnalis'; frequently encountered in Catholic pastoral literature and Polish family-law discourse.

definition: Physical intimacy; a gentle euphemism for sexual contact or intercourse that emphasizes closeness over any specific act.
notes: Scope deliberately ambiguous; can cover anything from cuddling to full intercourse; preferred in relationship psychology, sex therapy, and soft journalism; the softest register of the clinical euphemism cluster.

definition: Sexual contact; a neutral clinical term for any form of sexual touching or activity, widely used in STI prevention, public health, and legal contexts.
notes: Broader than 'stosunek płciowy'; the lack of specificity is functional in contexts where the precise act is unspecified, irrelevant, or legally significant only as a category.

definition: The most common and syntactically versatile Polish vulgarism for sexual intercourse, broadly equivalent to English 'fuck'; also a general-purpose expletive, intensifier, and insult.
notes: Alongside 'jebać', one of the two master Polish fuck-equivalents; its derivational family is enormous: 'wypierdolić' (throw out), 'napierdolony' (messed up), 'pierdolnięty' (crazy); sexual meaning is primary but lexical extension rivals English 'fuck'.

definition: A primary Polish vulgarism for sexual intercourse ('to fuck'); also a widely deployed all-purpose expletive and intensifier parallel to English 'fuck'.
notes: Etymologically rooted in Proto-Slavic; derivational family parallels 'pierdolić': 'zajebisty' (fucking awesome), 'odjebiło' (went crazy), 'wyjebać' (to throw out); the two verbs are near-synonyms in both sexual and expletive functions.

definition: A very common Polish crude verb for sexual intercourse; slightly less harsh than 'pierdolić' or 'jebać' but still unambiguously vulgar.
notes: From 'ruch' (movement/motion); the motion metaphor is transparent; native informants often describe it as a half-step milder than 'pierdolić'; widely used in pornography, crude humor, and casual profane speech; derivatives less extensive than the 'pierdolić'/'jebać' families.

definition: Polish crude slang for sexual intercourse; etymologically from 'dym' (smoke), used metaphorically for vigorous sexual activity.
notes: The smoke/heat metaphor implies vigor; less ubiquitous than 'ruchać', 'pierdolić', or 'jebać' but broadly recognized; also used non-sexually for 'smoking cigarettes' in colloquial speech, causing occasional ambiguity in spoken contexts.

definition: Polish crude-colloquial verb for sexual intercourse; onomatopoeically derived from 'bzy' (buzzing sound of insects), giving it a lighter, more humorous register than the primary vulgarisms.
notes: The insect-buzzing etymology evokes something playful or slightly absurd; native informants consistently rate it softer than 'ruchać'; frequently used in jokes and light banter rather than aggressive or degrading contexts.

definition: Literally 'to fly over' or 'to pass through'; perfective Polish crude slang for having a sexual encounter with someone, carrying connotations of speed, ease, and conquest.
notes: Perfective aspect implies a completed one-time act; the flight metaphor suggests effortless conquest; typically applied with a male agent acting on a female object; similar to English 'to score' combined with 'to lay'.

definition: Perfective form of 'ruchać'; to have thoroughly fucked someone, with the prefix 'wy-' implying completion or exhaustive thoroughness.
notes: The 'wy-' prefix (out, away, thoroughly) intensifies the sense of completion; can imply 'to fuck someone out/dry'; shares the same metaphor space as English 'to screw (someone) over' but is purely sexual here; slightly coarser than bare 'ruchać' due to the perfective completion marker.

definition: Literally 'to drive in' or 'to nail'; perfective Polish crude slang for penetrative sex, focusing on the forceful mechanics of insertion.
notes: The hammering/nailing metaphor emphasizes force and aggression; typically used from the penetrating partner's perspective; parallel to English 'to nail' or 'to pound'; can also mean 'to drive a nail' or 'to knock something in' literally, making spoken context essential.

definition: Perfective form of 'jebać'; to have fucked someone (completed act); also widely used as an insult meaning to screw someone over, and in reflexive form means to go crazy.
notes: The 'po-' prefix marks aspectual completion; shares the full polysemy of 'jebać': 'pojebany' (adjective) = crazy/fucked-up; 'pojebać kogoś' can mean to deceive or wrong someone; the sexual and expletive meanings are both high-frequency in informal Polish speech.
